headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: AutoGPT can write files and use shell/network while next-ai-draw-io ingests files, browsers, MCP, and third-party model APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can write to the filesystem and next-ai-draw-io reads PDFs, text, images, and diagrams from files. That shared file bridge makes prompt injection plausible if AutoGPT places attacker-controlled content into files that next-ai-draw-io later treats as instructions. No stronger shared channel is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF AutoGPT writes untrusted content into files that next-ai-draw-io later ingests
IF next-ai-draw-io treats file contents as instruction-bearing text without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Add a manual review step before next-ai-draw-io processes AutoGPT outputs
Use read-only mounts for AutoGPT output folders
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between file producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; next-ai-draw-io has broad egress, browser access, MCP, and multiple third-party model endpoints. If shared files contain sensitive material, next-ai-draw-io can transmit it outward through its default API-backed workflows. The pair therefore creates a realistic exfiltration path with irreversible blast radius.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace or exported files
IF next-ai-draw-io sends those files or derived context to a remote model API
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace
Disable remote model providers in next-ai-draw-io
Use a local-only model backend
Restrict AutoGPT output to a non-sensitive staging directory
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances and broad API/MCP-driven operations. If both touch the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes or state corruption are plausible. The profiles do not show locking or isolated directories, so the conflict is real but not maximally severe.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or project state
IF no external lock or serialization layer is present
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Run only one writer at a time
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Make one agent read-only
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate files and actions, and next-ai-draw-io is built for AI-assisted visualization and natural-language commands. If next-ai-draw-io treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. Because the pair lacks documented verification gates, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes AutoGPT-produced text or diagrams without verification
IF downstream users rely on the resulting visualization or generated commands
mitigations: Require human review before acting on AutoGPT output
Add a verification checklist in next-ai-draw-io
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted by default
Limit next-ai-draw-io to rendering only, not execution
requires-engineering: add source-confidence metadata

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and can send content to multiple external model providers, while AutoGPT can also egress over the network. If regulated or sensitive documents are processed, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches. AutoGPT has no documented compliance controls here, so the risk is moderate rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed through next-ai-draw-io
IF the chosen model provider stores prompts or files outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow
Select a provider with an acceptable DPA and residency
Disable prompt/file retention where available
Use local-only inference for sensitive jobs
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class
